title: What is the object type?
answer: In JavaScript, 'object' is a data type for storing collections of data and more complex values. The typeof operator returns 'object' for objects (including arrays and null, although typeof null === 'object' is a historical bug).

title: Explain arrays in JavaScript
answer: Arrays are ordered collections that can store any type of value, accessible by numeric indices starting from 0, and can grow or shrink dynamically.

title: What is typeof operator?
answer: typeof is an operator that returns a string representing the type of its operand, e.g. 'number', 'string', 'object'.

title: Explain equality in JavaScript
answer: == checks loose equality and performs type coercion. === checks strict equality (no coercion, both type and value must match). Use === for most scenarios to avoid bugs from coercion.

title: What is Scope in JavaScript?
answer: Scope determines the visibility of variables. Global scope is accessible everywhere. Local/function/block scope restricts visibility to within functions or blocks.

title: Explain what is Linear (Sequential) Search and when may we use one? JSPY
answer: Linear search checks each element in order until a value is found. Use it for small or unsorted collections.

title: Explain Values and Types in JavaScript
answer: Primitive types are string, number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol; all others are objects. Every value has a type.

title: What is let keyword in JavaScript?
answer: let declares a block-scoped variable, limiting its visibility to the block in which it is defined (unlike var, which is function-scoped).

title: Explain what is Binary Search JSJavaPY
answer: Binary search finds a value in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. It's much faster than linear search for large, sorted arrays.

title: Explain the same-origin policy with regards to JavaScript.
answer: Same-origin policy restricts scripts from interacting with resources from different origins (protocol, domain, port) to avoid security issues like data leaks.

title: Is there anyway to force using strict mode in Node.js?:
answer: Yes, add 'use strict'; at the top of your file to enable strict mode in that file.

title: Why would you use something like the load event? Does this event have disadvantages? Do you know any alternatives, and why would you use those?:
answer: The load event fires when all resources (images, CSS) are loaded. It's useful if you need everything ready but it can be late. DOMContentLoaded fires earlier, after the DOM is parsed, making it usually better. readystatechange is another alternative.

title: What is strict mode?:
answer: Strict mode changes JavaScript semantics: disables some features and throws errors for silent bugs. Enable by adding 'use strict' at the top of a script or function.

title: What's the difference between Host objects and Native objects?:
answer: Host objects are provided by the JS environment (e.g. window, document in browsers). Native objects (like Array, Object, Function) are defined by ECMAScript itself.

title: What language constructions do you use for iterating over object properties and array items?:
answer: For arrays: for, forEach, map, for...of. For objects: for...in, Object.keys(obj).forEach.

title: What are some of the advantages/disadvantages of writing JavaScript code in a language that compiles to JavaScript?:
answer: Advantages: better tooling, type safety, modern syntax. Disadvantages: extra build step, possible compatibility issues, sometimes harder debugging.

title: Explain event bubbling and how one may prevent it:
answer: Event bubbling is when events propagate up the DOM tree from the originating element to ancestors. Call event.stopPropagation() to prevent further propagation.

title: What does use strict do?:
answer: 'use strict' enables strict mode, catching common coding mistakes and preventing unsafe actions.

title: Why is it, in general, a good idea to leave the global scope of a website as-is and never touch it?:
answer: Modifying global scope can cause naming collisions, bugs, and conflicts with other scripts/libraries.

title: What is a Polyfill?:
answer: A polyfill is JS code that adds modern functionality to older environments that don't support it natively.

title: Explain Null and Undefined in JavaScript:Null:
answer: null is an assignment value for 'no value'. undefined means a variable hasn't been assigned a value. Both are primitive.

title: What's the difference between throw Error('msg') vs throw new Error('msg')?:
answer: No practical difference: both throw an Error object. Convention is to use new Error('msg'). If you omit 'new', Error('msg') still returns an Error object.

title: What is Callback Hell and what is the main cause of it? :
answer: Callback hell is nested callbacks that make code hard to read and maintain. It's caused by extensive use of asynchronous functions with callbacks.

title: Explain what is Interpolation Search JSPY :
answer: Interpolation Search estimates where a value might be in a sorted array using the value distribution. Fastest when data is uniformly distributed, with average time complexity O(log log n).

title: What is IIFEs (Immediately Invoked Function Expressions)?:
answer: An IIFE is a function that's executed immediately after it's defined, creating a private scope.

title: What is Coercion in JavaScript?:
answer: Coercion is when JavaScript automatically converts values to another type during operations. Can lead to unexpected results.

title: What is the difference between a shim and a polyfill?:
answer: A polyfill implements browser features you expect but may be missing; a shim is any code that adapts old APIs to new ones or vice versa, sometimes just providing a wrapper.

title: What is a Jump (or Block) Search? JSJavaPY :
answer: Jump search divides a sorted array into blocks of fixed size, jumping between blocks then linearly searching within one block. It's more efficient than linear search, less than binary.

title: What is the definition of a Higher-Order Function?:
answer: A higher-order function is a function that takes another function as an argument or returns a function.

title: What do you think of AMD vs CommonJS?:
answer: AMD loads modules asynchronously (for browsers); CommonJS is synchronous (for Node.js). AMD is better for browsers; CommonJS for server-side. Modern JS uses ES modules.

title: Explain the differences on the usage of foo between function foo() {} and var foo = function() {}:
answer: function foo() {} is hoisted and available anywhere in scope. var foo = function() {} is only available after assignment and is not hoisted as a function.

title: What is the drawback of creating true private in JavaScript?:
answer: True private variables are accessible only within their closure. Drawbacks: more complexity, can't easily extend/modify from outside.

title: What's the difference between .call and .apply?:
answer: .call() passes arguments as comma-separated, .apply() passes arguments as an array. Both let you set the function's this context.

title: What is the preferred syntax for defining enums in JavaScript?:
answer: JavaScript does not have native enums; use a frozen object: const MyEnum = Object.freeze({ VALUE_1: 'value_1', VALUE_2: 'value_2' });

title: Describe Closure concept in JavaScript as best as you could:
answer: A closure is a function that remembers its outer scope even after execution; allows access to variables outside its own body.

title: Could you explain the difference between ES5 and ES6?:
answer: ES5 (2009) is widely supported. ES6 (2015) introduced let, const, arrow functions, classes, modules, destructuring, and more modern syntax.

title: When should we use generators in ES6?:
answer: Use generators to make iterators, lazy sequences, or for custom asynchronous flow control code.
